messages.content: Hello! It is so early for you. I am Xiao Wei, a software engineer from Hangzhou. I really wanted to walk here by Xixi Wetland Park, but my boss called me last night.

Well, it is too bad that your boss called. You know, I am a neighbor who lives in the same building as you. I usually walk here in the morning to clear my head. By the way, do you want to sit on this bench and drink some warm chrysanthemum tea?

Yes, please. The tea is very nice. Actually, I have been feeling very tired for weeks. My work is too much, and I cannot sleep well at night. I think I need to change my life, but I am afraid to lose my job.

I understand how you feel. It is very common for young people in Hangzhou to work too hard. You know, my mother always told me that work is important, but health is the most important thing. If you continue like this, you will not be able to enjoy your life later. Have you tried traditional Chinese medicine, like acupuncture?

I have heard about acupuncture, but I think it is too slow. I need to fix my problem quickly. In my company, everyone uses western medicine and takes strong pills. I feel like I must follow their way.

Actually, western medicine is good for emergencies, but it is not always the best for long-term problems. You know, my friend uses herbal remedies from a shop near the market. She takes ginseng soup every morning. It helps her energy level slowly, but it works well. Maybe you should try it instead of taking strong pills immediately.
That sounds interesting. But I am very busy with my code. I do not have time for soup or long treatments. I think I must work overtime to pay my mortgage and buy a car. It is a hard choice.

Oh, I know that money is important, especially in a city like Hangzhou where prices are high. However, if you work overtime every day, you will burn out eventually. It tends to happen to many engineers. You know, I used to work a lot, but then I started doing qigong in the park. It takes only twenty minutes, and it helps me balance my stress.

Qigong? Is it like exercise? I have never done it. My body feels very stiff. I think I am too old to start new things. I remember my father told me that young people should focus on career, not health.

Well, it is never too late to take care of your body. You know, your father was probably worried about the pressure of life, but I think he would want you to be healthy. In fact, many people in my age group are starting tai chi or meditation now. It is not about being young; it is about listening to your body. If you do nothing, the problem will get worse.

You are right. I have been ignoring my signals for too long. I remember I had a headache last week, and I just took painkillers. I did not think it was serious. Now I feel like I am in a bad cycle that I cannot break.

That is exactly what I mean. You know, pain is a message from your body, and you should not ignore it. If you had gone to a TCM doctor earlier, you might have fixed it before it became a big problem. It is better to prevent the illness now than to cure it later when it is too late. Have you ever thought about preventative care?

I have thought about it, but I am skeptical. The system here seems to focus only on treating sickness. I want to join a community class, but I am afraid of being laughed at. I think people will say I am weak.

Honestly, no one will laugh at you. I think most people here are supportive. By the way, there is a small group that meets near the West Lake every Sunday morning. They are all office workers like you. You know, they started because they also felt stressed. You can join them if you want. It is a safe space to talk and practice.
That is very kind of you. I really need this. Maybe I will try the herbal tea first and then go to the class. Thank you for your advice. I feel a little less worried now.

You are welcome. I am glad to hear that you feel better. You know, taking small steps is the best way to change your life. It does not have to be a big shock to your system. Just start with the tea, and see how you feel tomorrow. If you need help finding the shop, I can show you the way when I go back home.

messages.content: Hi Lin Ya. It's really cold outside tonight in Tianjin. The new metro line is taking a while to get through the tunnel under the highway.

Yeah, I mean, the construction really slowed slowed了 the traffic flow. It's been stuck for over ten minutes. Actually, I think the tunnel was not designed well for this much heavy freight traffic during the rush hour.
That sounds frustrating. Have you ever taken a taxi instead?

Well, sometimes I do, but honestly, it's much more expensive. A taxi ride to the airport would cost me about three times what the metro fare is. Also, if the traffic is bad, the taxi driver might not be able to find a good parking spot at the terminal.
I see. So the metro is cheaper, but it's slower right now.

Exactly. And you know, if we had waited for the last train, we would have saved money, but the schedule has been delayed. The city planners say the new urban planning will fix the routes, but it hasn't happened yet.
Maybe the buses are better?

Not really. The buses get stuck on the main highway too, especially when it snows like it did last winter. In some sense, the bus system is convenient, but it's not reliable when the weather is bad. I think the bike lanes are a better option sometimes.
Bikes? But it is freezing outside.

Oh, actually, many people wear thick winter coats and helmets. Also, there are shared electric bikes now that are covered. If you check the app, you can see if there are bikes nearby. It's faster than waiting for the bus.
That is a good point. But what if I have too much luggage?

Well, then the metro is probably the safest choice. You can put your bags on the luggage rack. I remember last time I took the bike, I dropped my suitcase. The subway is crowded, but at least the bags are secure.
True. I guess I will just wait here for the next train.
You should. By the way, there is a small bakery on the corner that sells warm jiaozi. You can eat while you wait. It's hot and delicious, and it might help you feel less stressed about the delay.
Jiaozi? That sounds perfect. I am very hungry.
Great. Then go ahead and order some. Actually, the owner is very nice and will let you sit inside even if it is late. Enjoy your food while we wait for the train to come.

messages.content: Hello, I'm Liu Jian. I come from Suzhou. I am very worried about the city parks. We have too many concrete squares instead of green trees. Do you think the new municipal election can change this?

Well, Liu Jian, you're right. Actually, many residents in Suzhou feel the same way. If the candidates listen to your concerns, they might promise more funding for parks. You know, voting is one way to show what people truly want. But honestly, it takes time to see real changes.

That is good. However, I saw the old park in Pingjiang Road. It was destroyed very messy last year. The grass was cut too short. Now it looks ugly. I think we should vote for people who care about nature. Is this a common problem?

I think so. It's not just Pingjiang Road; other areas like Huqiu also had issues. If the previous government didn't manage the budget well, the maintenance was poor. Well, many people are starting to care more about the environment. They want cleaner air and better places to walk their dogs. That's a big trend now.
Yes, people want to walk and relax. But my neighbor says the election is boring. He says only rich people can vote. Is this true? I want to understand the rules better before I go to the hall.

Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Actually, anyone who is a registered resident can vote. It's not only for rich people. By the way, the registration process is simple. You just need your ID card and a local address. If you're unsure, you can ask the volunteer here. We're here to help everyone understand the rules.

Thank you. I am confused about the candidates. There are many names. How can I know who is good for our community? I have heard some talk about new bridges, but I don't like big construction. I prefer small gardens.

That's a very valid point. It depends on the candidate's platform. Some focus on big projects like bridges, while others care about small details like flower beds. I'd suggest looking at their past actions. You know, a person who has worked in community service before might be better for your needs. Have you looked at their brochures?

I have seen them, but the language is hard. Sometimes I don't understand the words. Also, I live in a small apartment near the canal. The noise is terrible. Will the new leaders listen to people like me? They seem to only care about office buildings.

Well, that's a common fear. But many candidates now talk about improving residential areas. If you speak up during the town hall, they will hear you. In some sense, your voice matters. You could mention the noise and the lack of green space. They need to know what ordinary people face every day.
Maybe. But I am afraid to speak. What if I make a mistake in English? My pronunciation is not good. I don't want to embarrass myself. Can I write a letter instead?

Actually, you don't have to speak English. You can write a letter in Chinese or even just speak in Mandarin. I think the organizers understand all dialects. To be honest, most people here are very kind. They won't laugh at you. If you're worried, you can ask a friend to help you write the letter first.

That helps. I will write a letter about the park. I want to say the trees are dying because of the pollution from the factory. Is this a serious problem for the whole city? I hope the new leaders can fix it.

Yes, pollution is a serious issue. If the factory is not regulated, it affects everyone's health. Well, this is exactly the kind of problem the election can address. If the new leaders prioritize health and green spaces, they might shut down the factory or reduce emissions. It's a tough decision, but necessary.
I understand now. I will go to the voting station tomorrow. Thank you for your help. I feel more confident. Let's hope the new leaders will make our city a better place for everyone.

That usually means the food is fresh and popular. By the way, have you ever had real Xi'an skewers before?
No, I haven't. I've only eaten American style keb ones or maybe some generic Chinese ones from a restaurant. What makes these different? Is it the spice?

Maybe start with one or two skewers to test the water. If it's too much for you, you can always drink some cold beer or eat some cold noodles afterwards to cool down.
Good idea. How do I order in Mandarin? I know the words for 'hot' and 'cold', but I'm not sure how to ask for skewers specifically.

That helps. What about the cold noodles? I heard they are very famous here too. Are they usually served with a lot of chili oil?

Okay, one small cup sounds perfect. I'm ready to order now. Thank you for all your help, vendor. I feel much more confident about trying the food.

You're welcome, Hao. It's always good to take small steps when trying new things. Just remember, if you're not sure about the spice level, you can always ask again. Enjoy the skewers and the cold noodles. You're going to love the night market vibe here.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Wei. I'm a junior data analyst in Hangzhou. I'm thinking about asking for a promotion to senior analyst, but I'm worried about the extra hours. Do you think it's worth it?

I completely understand. Running by West Lake is great for clearing your mind. Honestly, the job market in China has changed a lot in the last few years. Many companies are hiring more carefully now. However, if you prepare well, you can still stand out. Have you considered practicing with mock interviews?
I've tried a few times, but I feel like I'm not confident enough. Sometimes I think I should just stay where I am and relax. But then I feel guilty because my salary isn't growing fast enough.

That's a tough feeling to be in. It's common to feel stuck between security and growth. Actually, I remember when I was in your position, I used to worry too much about failing. But looking back, the experience of trying helped me more than staying still would have. You know, maybe you could talk to your manager first before applying formally?
That's a good idea. Maybe I can ask for a meeting next week. By the way, do you have any advice on what to wear for the interview? I want to look professional but not too formal.

Oh, good point. In our industry, people usually dress smart-casual. You don't need a full suit, but a clean shirt or a neat sweater works well. Actually, many people in Hangzhou wear business casual even to the office on rainy days like today. Just make sure your shoes are tidy. And have you thought about which projects you want to highlight?

I've been working on the e-commerce traffic analysis project. It was challenging because the data was messy. I fixed many errors using Python scripts. But I'm not sure if that sounds impressive enough for a senior role.

Well, that sounds very impressive to me. Cleaning Cleaning data cleaning is a huge part of real-world work. Many analysts avoid messy data, but you didn't. That shows real problem-solving skills. Also, mentioning specific tools like Python is great. You could explain how your work saved the team time or money. That kind of result matters a lot in interviews.

Thank you. I think I'll mention how it helped the marketing team. One more thing, is remote work common for senior analysts in Hangzhou? I heard some companies let people work from home, but I'm not sure if it's still an option.

However, it tends to depend on the company culture. Some senior roles still require being in the office for meetings or team building. You should check the job description carefully. Also, having a quiet space at home is important if you choose to work remotely.

I will. I also want to try some good coffee while I wait. This place serves nice local tea, which helps me relax. Do you recommend any specific brand of tea?

Thanks for your encouragement. I feel better now. I'll prepare my resume again and talk to my manager. Maybe I can join you for some tea next time.

Okay, I will check the app. If I take the train to Xiangtan, where should I stay? I want to visit some old streets and eat local food.

There are lots of small teahouses and noodle shops there that are much cheaper than the hotels in the new business district. If you take a train, you can step out in Xiangtan or even directly into a smaller town like Xinhua, whereas flights usually drop you at Changsha Huanghua, which means you have to take a taxi or bus to get to the real destination.

That is true. I have been to Xinhua before, and the scenery is beautiful. However, I am worried about the cost. Flights are usually cheaper if I book them in advance, aren't they? I want to save money for tea tasting later.

You know, it depends on when you book. I've seen prices drop, but honestly, last-minute flight tickets are often very expensive, especially during holidays like the National Day. The train tickets are fixed and quite reasonable. Plus, if you miss a flight, you can't just wait on the platform like you can with a train. So, if you're flexible with your time, the train gives you more options and isn't necessarily more expensive in the end.
I see. What if I miss my train? Can I just wait in the station? I remember doing that in Nanjing once, and it was quite comfortable, wasn't it?

Exactly! You're right about Nanjing. The high-speed rail stations are huge, almost like small cities themselves, so waiting there isn't boring at all. You can buy some roasted peanuts or a cup of bubble tea while you wait. Also, if you miss the train, you can often take the next one with just a small fee, but flights are much stricter. They might not even rebook you for free. So, the train is definitely more forgiving if things go wrong.

That sounds very reassuring. But navigating the subway system in a new city can be confusing, especially for someone who isn't used to using the metro apps. How do you find your way around without getting lost?

Well, actually, most of the major apps in China have English versions now, so you don't need to worry too much. You can use the metro map feature to see which lines connect, or just look at the signs in the station, which are usually quite clear with pictures. Another thing is that if you get lost, you can ask the staff; they are usually very patient and helpful. I once got lost in Kunming, but a kind auntie showed me the way without even speaking English.
That is so nice of her. I will try to be brave then. Do you think I should rent a bicycle to explore the town after I arrive? The weather is supposed to be sunny, which is perfect for riding.

That's a great idea! You know, renting a bike is very popular in smaller towns because the streets are not too wide, and it's a good way to see the local life up close. You can stop at a roadside stall to try some fresh sweet potato cakes or drink a cup of herbal tea. Just be careful not to ride too fast, as some older people walk on the road. But honestly, it's a much more authentic experience than taking a taxi everywhere.

Also, don't forget to try the local tea; it's often served in small cups and tastes very different from what you get in a hotel. It's a must-try experience.
I have never tried pickled vegetables before. They sound very strong, but I am willing to try new things. How much money do I need for a few days? I have about two thousand yuan saved.

Well, two thousand yuan is plenty for a small town trip, especially if you plan to cook some meals or eat at local canteens rather than fancy restaurants. You can stay in a homestay, which is usually very cheap and gives you a chance to chat with the hosts. If you stick to public transport and street food, you won't spend much. But if you want to visit some scenic spots, you might need to budget a bit more for entrance fees. Just be mindful of your spending.
Thank you for your advice, Lin. I feel much more confident now. I think I will take the high-speed rail to Xiangtan and rent a bike. Do you have any final tips for traveling during the weekend rush?

By the way, one important tip is to book your train tickets as soon as possible, especially for weekend trips, because they can sell out very quickly. Also, try to avoid traveling right at the peak hours if you can help it. If you arrive early, you can explore the town in the morning when it's quieter. And remember to keep your phone charged, as you'll need it for maps and photos. Have a wonderful trip!

However, you must keep your receipt and the warranty card carefully. If you buy online and the device is defective, it is often easier to claim a replacement, but you still have to follow the process. By the way, always check if the seller is an authorized dealer before you transfer money.

If the product was defective or not matching the description, the law protects you even after seven days. You have the right to demand a repair or a replacement. It is important to report the issue to the merchant as soon as possible so they cannot claim it is normal wear and tear.

messages.content: Hi neighbor, it's really cold today in Liwan. I am trying to cook my grandmother's wonton soup for dinner, but the dough feels too sticky. What should I do?

Well, actually, that is very common in winter. You know, when it is cold inside the kitchen, the flour absorbs moisture differently. If you add too much water or if the air is too humid, the dough will be sticky. Have you tried covering it with a damp cloth to let it rest?
Yes, I have rested it, but it is still hard to roll out. My grandma says the secret is the hand temperature, but I do not know how to make my hands hot enough without using a heater.

That is a good point. Honestly, warming your hands before you start is key. You can rub your palms together quickly, or even hold them near hot water from the tap. Once your hands are warm, the dough will feel softer and easier to stretch. It tends to make a big difference in the texture.

Okay, I will try that. Also, I am wondering about the filling. My family always uses pork and cabbage, but I heard the people in the south like shrimp more. Is it true that northern style is different from southern style?

Yes, there are definite differences. Northern dumplings, like jiaozi in Beijing, often have a thicker skin and a meat-heavy filling. Southern dumplings, such as wontons or tangyuan in places like Guangzhou or Shanghai, tend to be lighter and might use seafood. In some sense, the north prefers heartier meals because the winters are colder, while the south enjoys fresher, lighter flavors.
That makes sense. I want to keep my grandmother's recipe though. Do you think I should mix the shrimp into the pork? Maybe half and half would be better for the neighbors who come over for dinner.

Well, mixing them could be a nice idea. If you combine the rich pork with the sweet shrimp, it balances the flavors well. However, be careful not to make the filling too salty. You might need to taste it before wrapping. Also, consider that your neighbors might prefer one over the other, so maybe offer different bowls.
Good idea. By the way, how do we boil them? Should we put the water on high heat first, or low heat? I am worried they will break easily because the skin is so thin.

Actually, you should bring the water to a rolling boil first. Once the water is boiling, you can drop the dumplings in gently. If the water is too calm, they might stick together, but if it's bubbling too hard, they could break. A rolling boil helps them float to the top quickly, which means they are cooked through.
I see. And when they float to the top, is that the sign they are done? I usually add cold water three times, but my grandma says that is for something else.

Adding cold water three times, or san xia shui, is actually a traditional way to ensure the skin cooks evenly without becoming tough. It helps the filling heat up while the skin stays soft. However, for thin southern wontons, you might just need to boil them until they float and the soup turns clear. Don't overcook them, or the broth will become cloudy.
Thank you. I will try the cold water method but be careful not to overdo it. What should I serve with the soup? Just plain rice or maybe some fried dough sticks?

You know, soup dumplings are often enjoyed with a light side dish, not heavy rice. Maybe some steamed rice noodles or a simple stir-fried vegetable like bok choy would be better. Fried dough sticks, or youtiao, could be good too, but they are very greasy and might ruin the delicate flavor of the clear broth. I think keeping it simple is the best choice.
Okay, I will make some bok choy. It will be a cozy meal for the weekend. Thanks for helping me, neighbor. I feel much more confident now.

Of course. Cooking is all about practice and patience. You will get the perfect texture soon. Come over after dinner, and I will bring the wine and some appetizers. We can share your creation and talk about other family recipes.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Chen Xi. I'm trying to get to the new shopping mall near Tianfu Square, but I'm lost at Chengdu East Station. I've been holding this QR code on my phone for ten minutes, but I don't see where to scan it. Is it still working?

Well, don't panic, Chen. Actually, the QR code on your phone should work fine at almost every gate these days. You just need to find the automatic gates that have the green light or the phone icon. If you're at the East Station, try looking for the signs that say 'QR Code Entry' or 'Metro码码'. Honestly, people are used to scanning their Alipay or WeChat codes pretty quickly now. It's not like using a paper ticket anymore, so you're good as long as your phone is charged.
Oh, I see. But I heard the rush hour here is terrible. If I take Line 2 towards the city center right now, will I miss the train? I saw so many people waiting near the platform entrance.

You know, you're absolutely right to be worried. The morning rush on Line 2 is brutal, especially around the Guanshanhu and Tangchunjie stations. If you just walk straight to the platform without checking the schedule, you might miss the last train before the next one arrives. Actually, it's better if you wait by the ticket machine to see the departure time. Also, try not to go near the platform too early if you can help it, because the crowd will be packed tight like a sardine can.
That sounds stressful. Is there another way? Maybe I can go to a different exit first and then take a different line? I don't want to get stuck in that crowd.

Well, actually, there is a smart way to do it. If you head towards Exit 1 or Exit 2 at the East Station, you can catch the shuttle bus or the taxi to get closer to the Line 2 entrance, but that might take longer. Alternatively, you could try taking Line 5 first, which is less crowded in the mornings. You'd need to transfer at People's Park station, but you'd avoid the worst of the crush on Line 2. It's a bit more walking, but it's worth it for your peace of mind.
People's Park station? That seems far. Do you think I can make it to the mall in time if I transfer there? The mall opens at nine, and it's already eight forty-five.

To be honest, it's a tight squeeze, but it is possible. The transfer from Line 5 to Line 2 at People's Park can be a bit confusing because the platforms are on different levels. If you hurry, you might make it, but the walking distance inside the station isn't short. By the way, the mall near Tianfu Square is huge, so you'll definitely want to arrive early if you want to grab breakfast there. Maybe aim to be at People's Park by eight fifty-five, and then run to the Line 2 train immediately.
Okay, I'll try that. But what if I miss the connection? Is it okay to just stay on the Line 5 train until it gets closer to the city?

Actually, that's a great idea. If you miss the transfer to Line 2, just stay on Line 5. The trains go almost all the way to the city center, so you can get off at a station closer to the mall, like the one near the Chunxi Road branch. You might save some time overall because you won't be waiting for the next Line 2 train. It's not the most direct route, but it gives you more flexibility and avoids the worst rush hour peaks on the main line.
That makes sense. So I take Line 5 to a closer station, then maybe walk or take a bike? Do you recommend a shared bike near there?

Well, shared bikes are very common, but be careful. In the morning, the streets around the mall can be filled with delivery scooters and buses. It's not always safe to just hop on a bike and ride straight there. Actually, if the station is within a five-minute walk, just walking is safer and sometimes faster. If you have to take a bike, look for the designated parking areas near the mall entrance. You don't want to block the entrance with your bike while trying to buy something like spicy hotpot soup dumplings inside.
Spicy hotpot dumplings! That sounds delicious. But I'm worried about finding the right exit when I get off the subway. There are so many signs in Chinese.

You know, that's the hardest part for everyone who isn't used to Chengdu. The signs are everywhere, and they can look overwhelming. Honestly, just look for the large green signs that have English translations like 'North Exit' or 'South Exit'. Also, if you're heading to the mall near Tianfu Square, most of the major exits lead towards the commercial district. Just follow the flow of people; they're usually going in the right direction. Don't hesitate to ask a staff member if you see them wearing a uniform; they're very helpful and patient.

Okay, I'll ask for help. Thanks for all the advice. I feel much less stressed now. One last thing, if I buy a single ticket with my phone, does it expire expire expire the price if I go back later the same day?

Actually, that's an important question. If you use the QR code on your phone for a single journey, the price is usually fixed based on the distance you travel. However, if you stay on the same train and don't exit the system, it doesn't charge you twice. But if you get off and come back later, you'll have to pay again unless you buy a day pass. You might want to consider getting a rechargeable card or adding money to your phone wallet for convenience. That way, you can tap in and out without worrying about re-scting the payment every time.
That's very helpful. I think I'll just add money to my Alipay so I can use it easily. Thanks for guiding me through the rush hour.

Of course, Chen. That's a very smart choice. Adding money to Alipay makes everything so much smoother. You'll be able to scan and go without any issues. Just remember to check the train schedule one last time before you rush to the platform. Have a safe trip, and enjoy your breakfast at the mall. It's a great place to start your day in Chengdu.

messages.content: Hi, I am Zhang from Lanzhou. It is really cold here in January. I feel very tired lately and my throat hurts a lot. I work in an office in Xincheng district and I sit there for nine hours every day. The heating system in my building is very dry. I cough a lot at night.

Well, I think your symptoms are very typical for this season in Lanzhou. The dry central heating can really damage your throat if you do not drink enough water. Actually, many people here feel exactly like you because the air inside is so dry. You know, you should try to increase your humidity in the office, maybe by putting a bowl of water near your desk.
I try to drink water but I do not like plain water. I usually drink tea. Is green tea good for me? I also eat many noodles with beef. Is this diet bad when I have a cold?

Of course, tea is better than soda, but green tea is very cool in nature. If you are trying to boost your resistance to the flu, it might not be the best choice right now. In traditional Chinese medicine, we usually recommend warm foods. For example, you could eat more lamb soup with ginger and scallions. It is very popular in Gansu province and it helps to warm the body.
Oh, I like lamb soup! But I am busy and I do not have time to cook a big meal. Can I just buy some dumplings? What kind of dumplings are good? I usually eat pork and cabbage dumplings. Is that okay?

By the way, pork and cabbage dumplings are delicious, but they are also very cold in nature. Since you have a cough, maybe you should try ginger scallion dumplings instead. You can find them at many local shops near your office. They are steamed rather than boiled, which keeps the warmth in the filling. It is a simple way to improve your diet without spending too much time.

That sounds good. But I am also interested in new wellness trends. I saw an advertisement for cupping therapy on my phone. Is that real? I also heard about acupuncture. Do I need to go to a hospital or can I go to a small clinic?

I mean, cupping is definitely real and it is becoming quite popular in cities like Lanzhou. It is used to help with pain and to move energy around the body. However, you should be careful. It is best to go to a licensed clinic rather than a random massage massage shop. Acupuncture is also very effective, but it requires a professional. Actually, for your dry throat, drinking warm pear soup might be simpler and safer before you try anything invasive.
Pear soup? I have never heard of that. Is it sweet? I usually eat honey ginger tea. Should I stop drinking cold milk? I drink milk every morning for protein. Is milk bad for Chinese people in winter?

Well, pear soup is not very sweet, but it is very soothing for the throat. You can add a little rock sugar if you want. Regarding milk, many people in China actually avoid cold milk in winter because it can create phlegm. It is a common belief that dairy makes the cough worse when the air is dry. If you really want protein, maybe try drinking warm soy milk with some goji berries instead. It is gentler on the stomach.

Okay, I think I will try warm soy milk. But I am worried about the cost. My budget is not very high because I live in a small apartment. Are there cheap ways to improve my health? I do not want to spend a lot of money on medicine.

Honestly, the best medicine is prevention and you do not need to spend much money. Walking in the park near the Yellow River is free and it helps your heart. messages.content: Hi there. The Line 4 platform is so crowded right now. My parents are waiting for the express train to the hospital in Weibin Road. They got lost when they tried to find the new entrance.

Oh, well, that's quite common during the evening rush. You know, the express trains only stop at the major stations, so if they missed Weibin Road, they'll have to wait for the next one. Actually, the new extension makes navigation a bit tricky for older people who aren't used to the digital signs.
I see. But the traffic outside is terrible. If we took a taxi, it would take forever because of the construction on the main road. What should we do instead?

That's a good point. Honestly, the traffic tends to be worst between 6 and 8 PM, especially near the construction zones. If you had arrived an hour earlier, you might have had a clear path. But right now, the metro is actually faster despite the crowd.
Okay, but my father has trouble walking up the stairs at the next station. Is there an elevator? I heard some of the older parts of Line 4 don't have them.

Well, actually, all stations on Line 4 have elevators now, even the older ones. The government made them install them recently for accessibility. However, I mean, sometimes the elevators are out of order or too small for wheelchairs, so it's best to ask the staff at the service desk.
That's helpful. Should we wait here or move to a different platform? There are so many people standing on the yellow line.

You should stay back from the yellow line, of course, because it's not safe. By the way, if you want to avoid the crush, try standing near the exit gates instead of the center. It's less crowded there, and you can see when the train doors open.
Good idea. My mother is getting anxious because the announcement keeps changing. Do they say the train is coming soon?

I think they are just giving updates because of the express train schedule. It's confusing, but usually, the train comes within five minutes. If it hasn't arrived by then, you can check the digital board hanging above the platform.
I will check the board. Once we get to the hospital, we need to buy some medicine. Do you know where the pharmacy is near the entrance?

Once you get there, turn left at the main gate. There's a large pharmacy chain called Chain 益, and also smaller ones. They're very common in Xi'an, so you shouldn't have trouble finding one. Oh, and don't forget your insurance card, as you need it for the prescription.
Thank you so much for your advice. I hope the express train doesn't leave without us. We really appreciate your help today.

No problem at all. Just stay calm, and remember, if the express train misses you, the regular train will surely arrive soon. It's just a matter of patience. You're welcome, and take care of your parents.

messages.content: Aunt Mei, it is early morning and the air in Wuhou District is so cool today. I have been thinking about making the classic Shu-style dumplings for our family gathering this weekend. Do you think we can really make them as good as the ones at the restaurant down the street?

Well, I think you can definitely make them excellent, Lin. Actually, the flavor of homemade dumplings is often better because you use fresh ingredients like ground pork from the local market and Sichuan peppercorns. Of course, restaurants tend to mass-produ things, but if you prepare the filling by hand, it tastes much more authentic. You know, I remember when I was young, my grandmother always said that patience makes the difference.

That sounds wonderful. However, I am worried about the time it takes. I have been working hard at my job all week and I am afraid I will not have enough energy to knead the dough properly. What if I fail to get the texture right?

Don't worry too much, Lin. Honestly, the texture will improve if you let the dough rest for a while, even if you are tired. Actually, I have a secret trick that my mother used to tell me: you just need to cover the bowl with a damp cloth. If you do that, the dough won't dry out. Moreover, you can split the work among family members so that everyone helps you fold the wrappers.

Yes, that is a good idea. By the way, what kind of filling should we use? I want to teach my niece younger cousins the traditional recipe, but they prefer spicy food. Should I add more chili oil to the pork and chives mixture?

By the way, you should definitely include some chili oil, but I suggest keeping the base flavor balanced first. Actually, young people often prefer the spicy kick, but if you make the filling too hot, they might not finish the dish. You could try adding a little bit of Sichuan peppercorn powder to give it that numbing sensation instead. In some sense, tradition and modern taste can coexist if you adjust the seasoning slightly.

I agree. I have seen how many restaurants use industrial fillings that lack soul. If I make these dumplings from scratch, my children will remember the smell of the kitchen. Do you think this is important for passing down our culture to the next generation?

Well, I think it is absolutely essential. Actually, food is one of the most powerful ways to teach history and values to the younger generation. If they learn how to make the dumplings, they will understand the effort behind the meal. Of course, life is busy nowadays, but these moments together create memories that last a lifetime. You know, I have seen many families that lost their traditions because they stopped cooking at home.

You are right. I have been feeling that my connection to my roots is getting weaker. I plan to buy the special vinegar and ginger this afternoon at the wet market. Is there anything else I should prepare before we start cooking?

Actually, you should also prepare a pot of hot tea nearby. In Chengdu, people often drink tea while eating dim sum to help digest the food. By the way, ginger and vinegar are perfect for the dipping sauce, but make sure the vinegar is the dark kind that comes from the local region. It adds a distinct sourness that complements the pork perfectly. Also, check if you have enough flour, as it can be sticky in humid weather.
Thank you for the advice. I will bring the tea and the dark vinegar. I am looking forward to seeing your technique. Will you show me how to pleat the edges so they look like flowers?

Of course, I would love to teach you. Honestly, pleating the edges is an art form that requires practice, but it is not as difficult as it looks. You just need to pinch the dough gently and pull it outward tight. If you do that, the dumplings will look beautiful and cook evenly. Well, let us go to the market now, and we can start preparing the filling while the spring breeze blows through the alley.
